# nbzinbreg

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/jaxsonbugg/nbzinbreg/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jaxsonbugg/nbzinbreg/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

Negative binomial (NB) and zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) regression
in R, with the estimation written from scratch: iteratively reweighted least
squares (IRLS) and Newton-Raphson for NB, and the EM algorithm with IRLS steps
for ZINB. No general-purpose optimizer is used. NB results are validated
against `MASS::glm.nb()`, and ZINB results against `pscl::zeroinfl()`.

## Status

Negative binomial and zero-inflated negative binomial regression are
implemented and validated, with all required methods and the extras
(confidence intervals, model tests, bootstrap and diagnostics), and
benchmarked against `glm.nb()` and `zeroinfl()`, with a simulation study of
`zinbreg()`. The data analysis and report come next.

## Installation

``` r
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("jaxsonbugg/nbzinbreg")
```

## Usage

### Negative binomial regression

```{r nb-example}
library(nbzinbreg)
data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")

fit_nb <- nbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment, data = bioChemists)
summary(fit_nb)
```

### Zero-inflated negative binomial regression

```{r zinb-example}
library(nbzinbreg)
data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")

# Same covariates in both parts; use y ~ x | z to choose the zero-part
# covariates separately.
fit_zinb <- zinbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment, data = bioChemists)
summary(fit_zinb)
```

### Inference and diagnostics

```{r extras-example}
# Profile-likelihood interval for theta, Wald intervals for the coefficients
confint(fit_nb)

# Is there overdispersion? (Poisson against NB)
overdispersion_test(fit_nb)

# Observed against expected frequencies of the first few counts
head(expected_counts(fit_zinb), 4)
```

Model comparison with `anova()` and `vuong_test()` (including a bootstrap
likelihood-ratio test of NB against ZINB), bootstrap standard errors
(`boot_se()`), `simulate()`, `rootogram()`, and `tidy()` / `glance()` are
also available; see the function reference.

## Check results

`R CMD check`: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes on all CI platforms (macOS,
Windows and Ubuntu; R release, devel and the previous release). A local
Windows run may show one NOTE, "unable to verify current time", which comes
from the machine's clock check, not from the package.
